prompt: Write lambdas that capture surrounding values: makeAdders returns one adder per offset, makeLabeler returns a Supplier holding a prefix and id, and applyAll feeds a value through every operator in turn.
explanation: A lambda closes over the variables it mentions, storing a copy of their values at the moment it is created, which is why each adder keeps its own offset even after the loop has moved on. Java only allows this for effectively final variables, so copying the loop value into a fresh local inside the body (int captured = offset) is the standard move -- an enhanced-for variable is already effectively final per iteration, but the explicit copy makes the intent obvious. applyAll then shows the other half of the idea: functions stored in a list can be replayed later, long after the code that built them returned.
hints: Build an ArrayList inside makeAdders and add one lambda per loop pass: value -> value + captured.
makeLabeler needs no loop at all -- return () -> prefix + "-" + id and let the lambda capture both parameters.
applyAll keeps a running int, reassigning it to step.applyAsInt(current) for every step, and returns it at the end.
